commits.message:
fix(lanes): a bar pane is known by the command it was split with (candybar-launch-q7o7.0oo)

The split records the pane's owner in its argv (bar-pane <pane>), so finding
bar panes reads pane_start_command instead of a tag written after the split.
One plain split-window -d: no focus change, no chained commands to escape or
misname, and panes opened by earlier daemons are found the same way.
fix(lanes): a bar pane open gives focus back to the pane that had it (candybar-launch-q7o7.0oo)

fix(lanes): tag the bar pane by the split's own target, not a pane hook (candybar-launch-q7o7.0oo)

Pane-level after-split-window hooks fire only on tmux 3.8; earlier versions
accept and ignore them, so the pane went untagged. A split without -d makes
the new pane the queue's current target, which works from tmux 3.0 and leaves
no hook state to clean up.

fix(lanes): a bar pane is split and tagged in one tmux invocation (candybar-launch-q7o7.0oo)

A daemon closing between the split and its set-option refused the tag,
leaving a bar pane pane off could not find. A pane-scoped after-split-window
hook now tags the new pane inside the split's own command queue; a failed
split removes the hook so it cannot tag the user's next split.

fix(templates): the clock, payload reads, and edit-mode synthesis follow a dispatch into a partial (candybar-templates-zh8b.53s)

/code-review medium found 3 real gaps the first fix pass missed: render.ts's
instant-detection basis, render-payload.ts's payload-input closure seed, and
edit-mode.ts's toggle detector all still enumerated a segment's
template/bg/fg/when alone, so a clock read, a payload read, or an
`edit.toggle` reference reachable only through a dispatched partial was
invisible to each — the segment's own clock call threw at first draw, a
payload path never got fetched, and a toggle-only-in-a-partial reference
produced a confusing "unknown action" error instead of being synthesized.
All three now fold `seg.partials` in, the same way cross-ref.ts/
synthesis-inputs.ts/menu-synth.ts/unused.ts already do. Also: cross-ref.ts
and plugins.ts no longer hand-spell the same segment-template-field list
twice; plugins.ts now exports it once.

fix(templates): close gaps /code-review high found in partials (candybar-templates-zh8b.53s)

- cross-ref.ts: a partial reusing a global helper's name now a load error,
  not an uncaught "redefinition of template" throw at compile.
- merge.ts: a segment delta's partials merge by name over the base's, like
  settings, instead of wholesale-replacing (which silently dropped sibling
  partials a bundled template still dispatched to).
- unused.ts, synthesis-inputs.ts: both now walk a segment's partial bodies,
  so a helper/action/payload-read reachable only through one is no longer
  invisible to unused-detection or synthesis dependency tracking.
- menu-synth.ts: {{ menu }} inside a partial is now a load error too, for
  the same reason it already is inside a helper (the synthesis pass never
  follows a {{ template }} call into one).
- plugins.ts: a plugin segment's partials now go through the same
  self-binding/namespace pipeline (boundToSelf, fragmentTemplates,
  wrongScopeRefs, the tombstone-standin scan) as template/bg/fg/when.
- cross-ref.ts: collapsed the "is this name a helper or this segment's own
  partial" decision, previously implemented three times, into one
  helperKeyPath function both checkActionRefs and checkTemplateRefs call.
- dsl-types.ts: removed a stale lead/trail mention from the partials doc
  comment (those aren't SegmentDecl fields).

New tests pin all of the above in test/dsl-segment-partials.test.ts and
test/plugins.test.ts.

feat(templates): array-form segment templates and segment-scoped partials (candybar-templates-zh8b.53s)

A segment's `template` may now be an array of strings (joined with no
separator) for a long conditional that would otherwise be one unreadable
line, and a segment may declare `partials`: named sub-templates scoped to
it, compiled onto their own Defines chained from the shared `helpers`, so
two segments can reuse a partial name with no collision and a partial can
call a helper but never another segment's partial. Dispatch is via the
existing static `{{ template "name" ctx }}` builtin.

The dynamic `partial` function (a computed name) needs a capability
(`include`) that exists only on @promptctl/go-template-js's unreleased
master, not its published npm version — split into a follow-up ticket
(candybar-templates-zh8b.ph5), blocked on that release. Static unused-
partial detection needs unused.ts to carry per-template segment identity,
which it does not today — split into its own follow-up
(candybar-templates-zh8b.mfn), not blocked on anything upstream.

fix(test): the client-deadline cases state budgets a loaded loop cannot miss (brandon-unfiled-3248.5lkd) (#571)

The stub serves on the jest worker's own loop, so the statusline's 50 ms connect budget
could pass before its accept: the stated-budget case read CONNECT_TIMEOUT (1 of 20 runs
under CPU load), and the never-answers case passed without the request ever reaching the stub.
tryRenderViaDaemon takes its budgets as a value, defaulting to the wire facts the statusline
uses; the cases state wide ones, and the never-answers case asserts it ended at its own
deadline (TIMEOUT) having reached the stub.

* **test:** the click-error e2e holds its unanswered render until the daemon's side has ended (brandon-unfiled-3248.cbyb) ([#570](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/issues/570)) ([2b55ee9](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/commit/2b55ee999dbc13d1647e8946ffdb6557934b017a))

docs(design): the isolated daemon, tmux events and browser surface designs

Goals, architecture, contracts and one document per area, with the surveys and probes behind them. The Frame is recorded as built, and the browser surface is un-parked.
fix(bar-pane): a frame overwrites its rows and lands whole, so the pane stops flickering
